summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated 727 KB payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs` that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts the `bun`/`bun.exe` binary, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling `math_init.js` file. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB heavily obfuscated module using the standard shuffled-string-array pattern (`WV8StW` rotation routine, >500-entry constant table `n7gIxM`, hex-mangled identifiers) with a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header indicating it can only be executed by the Bun runtime — bypassing Node-based inspection. The `setup.mjs` dropper itself is obfuscated with hex-mangled import bindings (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and scrambled lookup tables that hide plain strings such as `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `powershell`, and `Expand-Archive`, indicating cross-platform installer-host reconnaissance and dispatch. The advertised functionality is a ~48-line ESLint rule at `dist/index.js`, which has no need for a second language runtime or a 727 KB payload. The combination of an alternate-runtime dropper delivered via preinstall, dual-layer obfuscation of both loader and payload, and a mismatch between the package's stated ESLint purpose and the downloaded execution surface is a supply-chain attack fingerprint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
